kicker: Chapter 21 · Fund it, or do not
title: Sell, don't issue: a worked example
subtitle: A UK company worth £10 million, a founder who owns all of it, an investor writing £2 million. The founder keeps 80% either way; in this model the investor buys 20% of the founder's shares.
alt: Arithmetic in four tiles: £2 million from the investor, minus about £420,000 in tax, leaves about £1.58 million; minus £0.75 million lent back to the company leaves about £0.83 million kept. Illustrative only; not legal, tax or investment advice; UK figures for one tax year.

tiles.label: about, in tax
tiles.detail: 18% on the first £1 million under Business Asset Disposal Relief from 6 April 2026, if its conditions are met, and 24% above

tiles.label: about, kept
tiles.detail: after tax and the loan; the buyer pays 0.5% stamp duty

note: Illustrative only: not legal, tax or investment advice; the UK figures are for one tax year and other countries differ. After tax and before the loan, about £1.58 million.
